network.help.reference.meaning: A snapshot used as the reference for other network readings.
network.help.reference.reading: To check for proxy or VPN bypass, use a snapshot captured on a known direct connection. Compare IPv4 with IPv4 and IPv6 with IPv6.
network.help.egress.meaning: The public source IP seen by the test site. IPv4 and IPv6 can use different routes.
network.help.egress.reading: Compare with a direct snapshot of the same address family. A direct IP match is a reason to check routing for that family.
network.help.ipv4.meaning: The public source address seen by the test site over IPv4.
network.help.ipv4.reading: Compare it with the direct IPv4 address and the expected proxy exit. Compare within the same address family.
network.help.ipv6.meaning: The public source address seen by the test site over IPv6.
network.help.ipv6.reading: Check IPv6 separately even when IPv4 uses a proxy. A missing reading means this test did not obtain an IPv6 result.
network.help.address.meaning: A connection source observed by the test site or an address mapped during a WebRTC test.
network.help.address.reading: Check the source shown below the address, then compare with the same source and address family in a direct snapshot.
network.help.organization.meaning: The network associated with the address, possibly including an operator and autonomous system number (ASN).
network.help.organization.reading: Use it to identify the exit or resolver network. One ASN can cover many regions and users.
network.help.region.meaning: The country, region or city estimated from the IP address.
network.help.region.reading: Use it as a rough location. A proxy or shared address may be located somewhere other than the device.
network.help.dns.meaning: The recursive DNS resolvers seen by the authoritative server for the test domain.
network.help.dns.reading: Compare with a confirmed direct resolver. Public resolvers can be shared, so interpret an overlap alongside the web exit and ECS.
network.help.ecs.meaning: EDNS Client Subnet. A resolver can send part of a client network to authoritative DNS, for example 203.0.113.0/24.
network.help.ecs.reading: Check whether the prefix contains your direct public IP. If the web exit changed but ECS still covers that IP, the test site still received information about the direct network.
network.help.ptr.meaning: A reverse DNS pointer record that maps an IP address to a domain name.
network.help.ptr.reading: The name may hint at an operator or hosting site. Treat it cautiously if forward resolution was not verified.
network.help.ns.meaning: An authoritative name server for the IP address’s reverse DNS zone.
network.help.ns.reading: Use it to identify who manages reverse records. Check the DNS resolver column for the recursive service observed handling queries.
network.help.webrtc.meaning: A public mapped address discovered through STUN during a WebRTC test.
network.help.webrtc.reading: Compare captures using the same STUN service. If WebRTC matches the direct IP of the same family while HTTPS uses the proxy, check WebRTC routing.
network.help.ice.meaning: Candidate addresses WebRTC can use to establish a connection, including local, mapped and relay addresses.
network.help.ice.reading: Read the address together with its type. host is local, srflx is server-observed, relay uses a relay server, and prflx is discovered by connectivity checks.
network.help.tls.meaning: The encryption protocol version negotiated with the test server, such as TLS 1.3.
network.help.tls.reading: Compare the version and handshake fingerprints on the same test site. A TLS-terminating proxy may establish the connection seen by the server.
network.help.http.meaning: The HTTP version observed by the test server, such as HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 or HTTP/3.
network.help.http.reading: A change may reflect negotiation or proxy behavior. Compare HTTP/2 fingerprints when both connections use HTTP/2.
network.help.ja3.meaning: A hash based on the TLS ClientHello version, cipher suites, extensions and their order, and related parameters.
network.help.ja3.reading: Compare on the same test site. Extension order alone can change JA3, so check JA4 and the proxy configuration as well.
network.help.ja4.meaning: Another TLS ClientHello fingerprint that sorts selected handshake fields to reduce sensitivity to ordering changes.
network.help.ja4.reading: If JA4 changes on the same test site, check the TLS version and proxy settings. A match means these handshake characteristics match and may be shared by multiple clients.
network.help.http2.meaning: A fingerprint based on HTTP/2 behavior such as SETTINGS, flow-control windows and request header ordering.
network.help.http2.reading: Compare only when both connections use HTTP/2. If a proxy terminates the connection, the site may see the proxy’s settings.
network.help.settings.meaning: HTTP/2 connection settings declared by the peer in a SETTINGS frame, such as header table size and initial flow-control window.
network.help.settings.reading: Compare the values and order of the same settings to investigate differences in the HTTP/2 fingerprint.
network.help.rtt.meaning: The estimated DNS round-trip time from the report.
network.help.rtt.reading: A shorter time means a faster response in this run. Congestion, distance and caching affect it, so compare trends across runs.
network.help.resolverIpv6.meaning: Whether the DNS resolver can query the test site over IPv6.
network.help.resolverIpv6.reading: Use it to assess resolver connectivity. Check the IPv6 web exit separately for browser connectivity.
network.help.adox.meaning: Encrypted transport from a recursive resolver to an authoritative DNS server, such as DNS over TLS or DNS over QUIC.
network.help.adox.reading: This reading describes the resolver-to-test-server connection. Check the browser-to-resolver connection separately.
network.help.edns.meaning: EDNS adds capabilities to DNS, such as advertising the UDP response size a resolver can accept.
network.help.edns.reading: Use the report to check EDNS support. Check ECS separately to see whether a client subnet was forwarded.
network.help.dnssec.meaning: DNSSEC uses digital signatures to verify the origin and integrity of DNS data.
network.help.dnssec.reading: Check whether the tested resolver rejects invalid signatures. Use the encryption test to assess whether DNS transport is encrypted.
